value.body: A healthcare quality executive helps a hospital meet accreditation standards and track how safely and consistently care is delivered. Hospitals working towards or holding NABH accreditation hire for this work. A typical day involves collecting quality indicator data from departments, auditing records and processes, and updating policies and SOPs.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BBA/MBA (Hospital Management), B.Sc Nursing or allied health

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Audit checklists, Excel, incident reporting systems

items.label: NABH-accredited hospitals
items.note: Hospitals with full NABH accreditation across all States/UTs
items.source: Rajya Sabha reply citing NABH data

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Many start in hospital administration or as a quality assistant, then move into the quality department. Short courses on NABH standards or internal auditing are commonly listed in job requirements.

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: quality manager, patient safety officer, accreditation consultant.
Some hospitals prefer a clinical (nursing) background for this role.
Work peaks around accreditation assessments and surveillance visits.

competition.note: BBA graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education

women.note: Share of women among BBA graduates in 2023-24 — the entry degree, not people already working in this role.
women.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education
